This page presents a comprehensive timeline of manned NASA space flights, organized chronologically from the Mercury program in 1961 to the final Space Shuttle mission in 2011. The main content is a large circular diagram that visually represents each mission as a spoke on a wheel, with the year of the mission indicated by its position. The timeline details key programs including Mercury, Gemini, Apollo, Skylab, and the Space Shuttle, listing specific missions, their dates, and notable achievements such as the first American in space and the first moon landing. A legend at the bottom identifies the different spacecraft types.

**Text Evidence:**
- The last Space Shuttle flight landed on July 21, 2011, ending 50 years of manned NASA flights.
- The US space program began in 1961 and resulted in 166 nearly continuous missions.
- The cost was an estimated $7 billion per year.
- The first international partnership in space was the Apollo/Soyuz Test Project in July 1975.
- The longest US space flight to date was Skylab 4, lasting 84 days, 1 hour, 15 minutes, and 31 seconds.
- The first human in space was Alan Shepard on Mercury Redstone 3 (Freedom 7) on May 5, 1961.
- The first person walked on the moon during Apollo 11 on July 20, 1969.
- The Space Shuttle Challenger exploded seconds after launch.
